chunks: 2765 - Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb narrated from al-Kāhilī, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about women in their ihram, and he said:

They may put in order whatever they wish to put in order. When they arrive at al-Shajarah, they enter ihram for hajj and recite the talbiyah at the milestone at the beginning of al-Baydāʾ. Then they are taken to Makkah, and they are hastened to the tawaf and the saʿy. When they complete their tawaf and saʿy, they trim [their hair], and mutʿah becomes valid. Then they enter ihram on the Day of al-Tarwiyah for hajj, and it is an ʿumrah and a hajj. If they fall ill, they remain upon their hajj and do not make their hajj separate.

key_terms.أَهْلَلْنَ: they entered the pilgrimage consecration with the hajj intention
key_terms.إِحْرَامِهِنَّ: their state of ihram for the pilgrimage rites
key_terms.السَّعْيَ: the ritual walking between Ṣafā and Marwah
key_terms.الشَّجَرَةَ: al-Shajarah, the miqat point where ihram is entered
key_terms.قَصَّرْنَ: they shortened or trimmed their hair to exit ihram
key_terms.لَبَّيْنَ: they recited the talbiyah in response to the divine call
key_terms.مُتْعَةٌ: tamattuʿ, the form of hajj combining ʿumrah followed by hajj

ai.seo_question: How should women in ihram perform tamattuʿ hajj according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding women in ihram, outlining how they proceed through the rites of tamattuʿ hajj. It explains their entering ihram, talbiyah, tawaf, saʿy, trimming, and renewed ihram for hajj, while also addressing the case of illness and maintaining continuity in their hajj.
